$comment: LICENSE-PENDING — see docs/non_ratified/LICENSE_PENDING.md. FirmwareArtifact per FB-RAT-DEV-002 (device object model). Typically carried as the `payload` of a ContractEnvelope<FirmwareArtifact> (see schemas/common/envelope.schema.json). `firmwareArtifactId` is this object's own FB-RAT-COM-002 stable ID.
title: FirmwareArtifact
description: A firmware image that can be flashed to a device: the underlying byte artifact (digest, storage, verification, build provenance — reused wholesale from schemas/common/artifact-ref.schema.json, not redefined), which boards it is compatible with (FB-RAT-DEV-007 wrong-board block needs this), its memory-layout expectations, and its signing status. See docs/ratified/DEVICE_STATE_AND_SAFETY_SPEC.md §2/§4.

firmwareArtifactId.description: Globally unique stable ID for this firmware artifact (FB-RAT-COM-002), independent of `artifact.id` — the two are typically equal but are named separately because a FirmwareArtifact can in principle wrap a pointer to an ArtifactRef minted by a different producer (e.g. a build system) without adopting that producer's id scheme wholesale.

artifact.description: The underlying byte artifact — digest (FB-RAT-COM-005), sizeBytes, storageLocation, verificationState, and producerReceipt (FB-RAT-COM-008 build provenance — 'build receipt' in the object model brief), reused as-is from schemas/common/artifact-ref.schema.json. Not redefined here.

boardCompatibility.description: FB-RAT-DEV-007 (wrong-board block): the boards this firmware image is declared compatible with. Non-empty — a firmware artifact with no declared compatibility target cannot be structurally checked against a DeviceIdentity.board before erase, which is exactly the check FB-RAT-DEV-007 requires; see fixtures/devices/adversarial/wrong-board-attempt.adversarial.json for the DeviceOperation-level fixture exercising the mismatch this field enables detecting.

unknownFields.description: Bag for fields a decoder received but did not recognize, preserved for round-trip (FB-RAT-COM-003).

catalogRef.description: FB-RAT-DEV-009: interoperate with Arduino CLI/PlatformIO metadata, never own a separate board catalog. Duplicated locally from schemas/devices/device-identity.schema.json's $defs/CatalogRef per this repo's convention (docs/ratified/COMMON_CONVENTIONS.md §5) of duplicating small shared sub-shapes across schema files rather than cross-file $ref'ing into another document's $defs.

catalogId.description: The catalog's own board identifier, e.g. an Arduino CLI FQBN ('arduino:avr:uno') or a PlatformIO board id ('esp32dev').

BoardRef.description: A DeviceOperation's wrong-board check (FB-RAT-DEV-007) compares a DeviceIdentity.board entry against this array using (catalogRef, catalogId) when catalogId is non-null on both sides, falling back to displayName equality only when either side is UNCATALOGED — this matching rule is documented here because a JSON Schema structural constraint alone cannot express cross-object matching; docs/ratified/DEVICE_STATE_AND_SAFETY_SPEC.md §4 states it as a provider-gate obligation.

flashBytes.description: Size in bytes of the flash region this firmware image is expected to occupy — a flash preflight (step 3) compares this against the target board's known flash capacity, when that capacity is available from the board catalog.

flashStartAddress.description: Hex-string flash start address, when the target protocol requires one to be specified explicitly (e.g. some DFU/UF2 targets). Null when the protocol/board pairing determines this implicitly.

signed.description: Whether this firmware image carries a cryptographic signature at all. Most hobbyist/embedded firmware (Arduino sketches, ESP32 app images built locally) is legitimately unsigned — `signed: false` is an expected, common, non-error state, not a defect.

signatureScheme.description: Free-text signature scheme identifier when signed=true (e.g. 'ESP32 Secure Boot V2', 'STM32 X-CUBE signed image'). Null when signed=false.

verified.description: Whether the signature (when present) has been independently verified against a trusted key by this constellation, as opposed to merely being present. Null when signed=false, or when signed=true but verification has not yet been attempted.
